main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) in olive green with sparse lighter and darker tufts; no standing volume
top_band: none - terrain tile with no standing object; a single flat green ground surface seen from above
evidence: The candidate is a seamless grass ground patch, which is terrain rather than a standing object. The 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply, and there is no object body, lid, or front face to judge. Reading a pixel column shows only repeating grass texture with small light and dark tufts. No side faces or elevation drawing are present. Terrain is exempt from the standing-object structure test, so Part A passes.

style.evidence: The candidate is mid olive green with sparse tufts in a light green and a dark green, so there are about 3 lightness steps against the reference grass, which has 5 or more with clumps, blades and a dark shade patch. Most of each tile is one flat base green. The tufts repeat in an identical pattern every 4-5 tiles, which reads as a mechanical stamp rather than hand-shaded variation. A faint grid-like noise exists, but it is very low contrast. Compared with the reference grass, which has varied blade strokes and richer tile content, each tile carries only about 3-4 colours, so density is much lower and the piece looks thinner and flatter. It has no outlines, which is fine for ground.
